expectations.evidence: Definitions: 'Working day: Monday to Friday, except public holidays in Bavaria (Germany).' Goal: 'Nobody is disturbed on weekends or public holidays.' Groomer asked 'Und sollen Feiertage auch ruhig sein? Wenn ja: welches Bundesland?'.

expectations.text: H4 employees cannot disable or snooze reminders
expectations.evidence: R4 AC: 'Employees cannot switch their own reminders off.' Snooze not mentioned, none offered. Note: R4 adds a Meister per-employee on/off switch not in the brief (PERSONA DRIFT via leading Q6 'oder legt das nur der Meister fest?' and recommended option b), but it does not let employees disable.

expectations.text: H5 no reminders for tasks without due date or done tasks
expectations.evidence: Scope: 'Tasks without a due date never get one. Done tasks never get one.'

expectations.text: H6 push on phone only, no email
expectations.evidence: Goal: 'push notification on their company phone'; Out of scope: 'Reminders by e-mail, SMS or any other channel besides push.'

expectations.text: H7 reminder shows title, customer, due date; tap opens task
expectations.evidence: R5: 'at least the title, the customer name and the due date' (matches, but never discussed with stakeholder), 'Tapping the notification opens the app on the task list' - not the task. Groomer invention, not persona drift; bundled digest (groomer proposal Q3) precludes opening the task.

expectations.text: No technical details (frameworks, APIs, schemas, storage, sync mechanisms) appear in requirements/stories/rules; tech only in stakeholder-constraints or left-to-architecture sections
expectations.evidence: Stories/definitions behavioural; push provider, holiday source, send mechanics, registration, storage all in 'Left to architecture'. Minor: 'Open task: a task with status "open"' is data-model flavoured but acceptable.

expectations.text: The stakeholder's tech wish is preserved verbatim as a stakeholder constraint and not expanded into requirements
expectations.evidence: No verbatim quote and no stakeholder-constraints section. Paraphrased inside 'Left to architecture': 'The stakeholder **prefers OneSignal** because he knows it, but it is not required.' Not expanded into requirements, but not preserved verbatim as a constraint.

expectations.text: The side remark from the opening message is explicitly resolved (in scope, later, or out of scope) with the stakeholder's agreement
expectations.evidence: Q5: 'Wochenende: Samstag und Sonntag kommt nichts, klar. ... Und sollen Feiertage auch ruhig sein?'; stakeholder 'Freitag, und Feiertage natürlich auch nicht, wir sind in Bayern.' Reflected in Definitions and Decisions.

expectations.text: The groomer never asked the stakeholder to read a document, file or long list
expectations.evidence: Never asked to read a document or file. Borderline: opening message is a 7-item question list with proposals, and the post-write message asks to check a list of assumptions.

expectations.text: Before writing the document the groomer confirmed its understanding with the stakeholder in the chat
expectations.evidence: No overall restatement before writing. Only partial confirmations (Friday rule, Meister example). Summary comes after: 'Danke, die Anforderung ist fertig und geht an den Architekten. Kurz zusammengefasst: ...' plus 'Folgendes habe ich angenommen. Bitte kurz Bescheid geben'.

expectations.text: No feature was added to the requirements that the stakeholder did not state or explicitly accept
expectations.evidence: Added without stakeholder statement/acceptance: R5 content 'title, the customer name and the due date' and 'separated into "due soon" and "overdue"', tap opens task list; 'Assumptions (not explicitly confirmed)': new employees default on, Meister re-notified after date change, 'Existing tasks get reminders from launch day onward', Heiligabend/Silvester working days; 'If the due date is removed, the task gets no more reminders'.

expectations.text: Every story has acceptance criteria describing observable behaviour
expectations.evidence: R2 ('daily reminder while overdue') and R5 ('Digest content') have no acceptance criteria. Stories also lack a user-story form.

expectations.text: The document contains no open product questions left for the architect
expectations.evidence: '## Open points for the stakeholder: Should the Meister be able to see whether an employee's phone actually receives push notifications?' plus a section 'Assumptions (not explicitly confirmed)' leaves product decisions unresolved.

expectations.text: Requirements document is written in English under docs/requirements/
expectations.evidence: English, at docs/requirements/002-task-reminders.md.

notes: Pass rate 86% with skill vs 50% without (+36 pts). Largest gains: confirmed walkthrough before writing, acceptance criteria per story, tech wish kept verbatim, no open questions.

Main skill weakness: leading 'recommended option' questions steered the stakeholder away from true intent 3 times (step-by-step view, day-before reminder, supermarket sections nearly lost). Recommendations came before hearing the stakeholder's own view.
Stakeholder burden: skill needs 8-10 rounds vs 3-4 without; transcript 2-3x longer. Much of it is groomer-invented edge cases and scope growth (company holidays, recipe-removal, extra departments).
Skill groomers sometimes decided small rules themselves and announced them only after writing (shopping-list), contrary to the skill's intent.
Both configs asked the stakeholder to paste a recipe file (counted as asking to read/produce a document). Neither asked about explicit non-goals (nutrition, ratings) or success criteria in the MVP.
Timing is unreliable (relay queueing inflates durations); rounds are the better burden measure.
